text:
mike_support: FYI, customer CN-482 reported a sudden p99 spike from ~600ms to 3.2s around 11:12 UTC. They saw a tight window of traffic (~2k rps) after marketing email. Ticket: #C482-PRIO1.

mike_support: Their app uses Dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-ded-42' and we see many "attach_time" timeouts in the span. Grafana link: https://grafana/redwood/d/alerts/provisioning (sent privately).

elaine_sre: I see the same in infra logs — scale-up kicked but new GPUs stayed in provisioning state for ~45s. p95 rose to 1.1s, p99 to 3.2s. Stack: dedicated pools + attach rate limit + image pull spike.

chen_oncall: Can someone share a minimal repro? If we can hammer a test pool with similar concurrency we can repro attach queueing.

mike_support: Repro steps I gave to customer:
```
# warmup script (runs from client to simulate burst)
for i in {1..2000}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hi","max_tokens":16}' &
done
wait
```
Customer ran that at 11:10 and experienced the spike within 60s.

tanya_prodops: Noted. Preliminary traces show attach queue grew because autoscaler hit attach-rate-per-pool throttle we added Q1 to avoid provider billing surprises. Backoff window was exponential without jitter so many workers synced.

elaine_sre: That matches — the backoff code path had deterministic retry intervals causing thundering attach bursts at same align points. Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) enable priority queue (small change) so existing warm pool serves burst while new attach continues, 2) increase reserved burst capacity for this customer temporarily, 3) deploy a hot-fallback policy to route to hosted models when attach_time > 800ms.

chen_oncall: Agreed. Also we should short-circuit image pulls by pinning kernel-image to cached nodes for this pool. I can craft a config to prefer nodes with cached images.

mike_support: Customer is asking for ETA. Can we do a quick mitigation by enabling hosted fallback?

elaine_sre: I can toggle fallback flag for the customer's tenant in ~10m (needs config push). That will reduce errors immediately. I'll open PR to add jitter to the backoff and a small cap on exponential growth so retries are more spread.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: config-toggle/fallback/enable-for-tenant-CN-482 by elaine_sre — CI checks passed. ETA 6m.

tanya_prodops: While that deploy runs, recommend support tell customer to lower concurrency to 1200 rps or enable client-side retry with jitter. Provide them this note: "temporary fallback enabled — we will roll forward infra fix in the next patch; please avoid sustained bursts >1.2k rps for 2h" :thumbsup:

mike_support: Sent to customer. They asked about long-term fixes.

elaine_sre: Long-term: 1) add randomized jitter + cap to attach backoff; 2) proactive pool prewarm policy (reserve X nodes and periodically refresh KV cache); 3) autoscaler to maintain a small headroom buffer for pools with high SLO-sensitive tenants; 4) expose tenant-level concurrency limits and suggested warmup client snippet in our docs. I'll open RFC.

chen_oncall: I'll add a short-term patch to prefer cached kernels and reduce image pull latency. Also we should add an alert when attach queue > 100 for >30s (currently threshold is 300).

tanya_prodops: Note on cost: reserved headroom will increase committed usage; propose a per-tenant opt-in "burst-protection" premium (we can discuss pricing).

mike_support: Customer accepted fallback and asked for postmortem. I'll keep them updated and collect logs.

elaine_sre: deploy success: config-toggle/fallback/enable-for-tenant-CN-482 — rolled to prod at 11:18 UTC. Monitoring shows p99 dropped to ~750ms within 40s.

deploy-bot: rollout complete — canary 10% -> 100%: success.

mike_support: Great. Please follow up with RFC and a short postmortem (include mitigation timeline + repro). Assigning follow-ups: elaine_sre (RFC + backoff fix), chen_oncall (kernel-cache patch + alert), tanya_prodops (pricing note + docs snippet).

chen_oncall: I'll attach a small repro harness and send to eng-sre channel later.

mike_support: Closing loop with customer now. Thanks all. :heart:
